name: Bible
tagline: 139 public-domain Bibles, offline from the first verse — the file is the save.
description:
Open it on a plane. Two English translations (the World English Bible and the King James) are inside the app from the first moment. The other 137 — 63 languages — download once when you first open them and then work forever with no account and no connection.

Read in paragraphs or stacked verses. Put a second translation beside the first, even across languages; when they number the psalms differently, the app maps them and says so. Tap a verse to highlight it, write or speak a note, hear the chapter read aloud, or open the study apparatus: the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge, Matthew Henry, Strong’s dictionaries, and a Hebrew or Greek interlinear.

Invite someone and you read the same page. Highlights and notes stay yours. Save keeps them in the file itself — hand that file to anyone and the marked-up Bible opens on their screen.

Every translation here is in the public domain. Place data © OpenBible.info (CC BY 4.0). The Hebrew interlinear is the Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (CC BY 4.0).
